title: WHEN NOISE LOWERS THE LOSS: RETHINKING LIKELIHOOD-BASED EVALUATION IN MUSIC LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Injecting controlled white noise and order shuffling into musical sequences (audio tokens) and analyzing token-wise loss dynamics to measure the model's inability to penalize long-term structural degradations, observing how it adapts to out-of-distribution errors.

Comparing the sequence likelihoods (loss values) of clean generated music against systematically corrupted music (noise-injected or shuffled) to show that models paradoxically assign lower loss to structural noise.
